scenes.tts: Turn a newt's eye upside down and let its nerve regrow. Why does it never learn to aim again?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Rank Against a Slope. A newt in profile, one eye marked with a rotation arrow. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Turn a newt's eye upside down and let its nerve regrow. Why does it never learn to aim again?

scenes.tts: In nineteen forty-three, Roger Sperry rotated the eyes of adult newts. He cut the optic nerve and let it regrow.
scenes.caption: In 1943, Roger Sperry rotated the eyes of adult newts. He cut the optic nerve and let it regrow.
scenes.visual: An adult red-spotted newt; the eye turns 180 degrees in its socket; the optic nerve is cut and slowly regrows. Label: Sperry, 1943.
scenes.narration: In 1943, Roger Sperry rotated the eyes of adult newts. He cut the optic nerve and let it regrow.

scenes.tts: When sight returned, a lure held above its head made it turn its head downward.
scenes.visual: A lure dangles above the newt; the newt turns its head down, away from the lure. A red arrow marks the wrong direction.
scenes.narration: When sight returned, a lure held above its head made it turn its head downward.

scenes.tts: If the fibres regrew at random and use then matched them, what should weeks of missed prey teach?
scenes.visual: The newt misses the lure again and again; a calendar flips through weeks. Question on screen: random wiring, matched by use?
scenes.narration: If the fibres regrew at random and use then matched them, what should weeks of missed prey teach?

scenes.tts: To aim correctly. It never learned. It kept making the mistake for as long as anyone watched.
scenes.visual: The calendar keeps flipping; the newt still turns downward each time. Label: never corrected.
scenes.narration: To aim correctly. It never learned. It kept making the mistake for as long as anyone watched.

scenes.tts: Sperry favoured the simplest reading: each regrown fibre went back to its old place in the brain.
scenes.visual: Regrowing fibres from the rotated eye find their original target sites, drawn as matching coloured dots.
scenes.narration: Sperry favoured the simplest reading: each regrown fibre went back to its old place in the brain.

scenes.tts: That place is part of a map. Neighbouring cells in the retina connect to neighbouring places in the target.
scenes.visual: Five coloured axons run from a retina strip to a target strip, keeping their order. Target labels: optic tectum (fish, amphibians, birds); superior colliculus (mammals). Orientation throughout: retina strip on the left, nasal at top, temporal at bottom; target strip on the right with anterior (front) on the left of its own bar.
scenes.narration: That place is part of a map. Neighbouring cells in the retina connect to neighbouring places in the target.

scenes.tts: Temporal retina, the side nearer the temple, maps to the front. Nasal retina maps to the back.
scenes.visual: Gold temporal axons end at the anterior end of the target; slate nasal axons end at the posterior end. Labels: temporal to anterior, nasal to posterior.
scenes.narration: Temporal retina, the side nearer the temple, maps to the front. Nasal retina maps to the back.

scenes.tts: A growth cone, the moving tip of an axon, senses only what is close. Yet the map spans the target.
scenes.visual: Zoom on one growth cone with a small circle of reach around it; pull back to show the whole target.
scenes.narration: A growth cone, the moving tip of an axon, senses only what is close. Yet the map spans the target.

scenes.tts: So how does an axon know where to stop? Three ways are possible.
scenes.visual: Three empty panels appear side by side. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: So how does an axon know where to stop? Three ways are possible.

scenes.tts: Labels: one matching tag for each cell and each target site.
scenes.visual: Panel one: numbered tickets matched to numbered seats.
scenes.narration: Labels: one matching tag for each cell and each target site.

scenes.tts: Gradients: a smooth slope in the amount of a molecule gives each position a value.
scenes.visual: Panel two: a shaded slope from light to dark across the target.
scenes.narration: Gradients: a smooth slope in the amount of a molecule gives each position a value.

scenes.tts: Neighbours: each axon places itself relative to the axons around it.
scenes.visual: Panel three: people lining up by height, tallest at the front. Label: neighbours = the other retinal axons arriving in the target.
scenes.narration: Neighbours: each axon places itself relative to the axons around it.

scenes.tts: In chick and mouse, the retina uses gradients and neighbours together.
scenes.visual: Panels two and three glow and slide together; panel one fades.
scenes.narration: In chick and mouse, the retina uses gradients and neighbours together.

scenes.tts: Each axon carries an amount of a receptor called Eff A. The target carries a slope of a repellent, eff-rin A.
scenes.caption: Each axon carries an amount of a receptor called EphA. The target carries a slope of a repellent, ephrin-A.
scenes.visual: Retina strip shaded for EphA, darkest at the temporal end. Target strip shaded for ephrin-A, light at the front, dark at the back. Labels: EphA, ephrin-A.
scenes.narration: Each axon carries an amount of a receptor called EphA. The target carries a slope of a repellent, ephrin-A.

scenes.tts: The repellent is low at the front and high at the back. The axon with the most receptor ends where it is lowest.
scenes.visual: The darkest-EphA axon keeps a branch tuft at the light front of the target; no growth cone is shown halting. On screen: more receptor, less ligand.
scenes.narration: The repellent is low at the front and high at the back. The axon with the most receptor ends where it is lowest.

scenes.tts: More receptor, less ligand. But where each axon lands also depends on the other axons.
scenes.visual: Axons line up by receptor level, then form branch tufts along the shaded slope. Label: coarse front-to-back map, chick and mouse; a simplified model.
scenes.narration: More receptor, less ligand. But where each axon lands also depends on the other axons.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: an axon's place is not an address in its own receptor level. It is a rank, set against a slope.
scenes.visual: On screen: a rank set against a slope, not an address in the receptor level alone. Small label: coarse front-to-back map, chick and mouse. The target strip stays shaded behind it.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: an axon's place is not an address in its own receptor level. It is a rank, set against a slope.
